newsitem.title: INDIA: Nestle India says interest costs surge.
newsitem.headline: Nestle India says interest costs surge.

text.p: Nestle India Ltd, a subsidiary of Switzerland's Nestle SA, said on Monday that interest costs and depreciation in the first half of 1996 rose substantially compared to the same period last year.
Interest costs surged to 261 million rupees in the first six months of calendar 1996, up from 119 million in the same period in 1995, the company said in a statement announcing first-half results.

"Interest cost has risen sharply on account of higher funding needs to service projects recently commissioned as well as export orders already in hand but to be executed during the latter part of 1996," the food company said in a statement.

The statement announced that net profit during the first six months of calendar 1996 was virtually unchanged at 223 million rupees, compared to 222 million in the same period in 1995. Net sales rose 23 percent to 5.1 billion rupees.
Nestle India, 51-percent owned by Nestle SA, said depreciation jumped to 118 million rupees from 73 million due to the capitalisation of several projects.
It said that following extremely good response to its Kit Kat chocolate bar, the firm was expanding the manufacturing capacity of its Kit Kat factory in Ponda.

Nestle said a plant to manufacture the chocolate food drink Milo had been commissioned in Nanjangud, and the initial response to tests of the product in the southern state of Tamil Nadu was encouraging.

Construction of a new factory in the western state of Goa for the manufacture of a range of products such as Instant Noodles, Sauces and Sandwich Spreads was progressing satisfactorily, the company said.
The firm paid an interim dividend of 2.50 rupees per share in June, it said.
